label: EU(7)-PIM: chloral hydrate
title: Chloral hydrate in an older person
statement: Chloral hydrate is on the list of medicines to avoid in older people because of the risk of dizziness and changes on the heart tracing. The European list describes greater risk with reduced kidney function and suggests a reduced dose for the shortest possible time. Australian product information for Orion Chloral Hydrate Mixture lists marked renal impairment as a contraindication and limits use for sleep disorders to two weeks.

plain_summary: Chloral hydrate, an old sleeping medicine, can cause dizziness and heart tracing changes in people aged 65 or over.

medicine_groups.name: Chloral hydrate
medicine_groups.note: A compounded liquid can also be recorded by ingredient. Orion Chloral Hydrate Mixture is registered in two strengths, 500 mg/10 mL and 1 g/10 mL. Read the strength from the dispensing line.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when the person is aged 65 or over and chloral hydrate is supplied, even once. If chloral hydrate is supplied and age is missing, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the patient is 65 or older. A recorded age below 65 rules out the finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why it was started, kidney function, heart tracing results, how long it has really been taken, and how much is really taken.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether chloral hydrate is still needed and whether a safer choice or a non-medicine approach for sleep is possible.
